title: Codex vs Claude Code vs Cursor vs Copilot — Best AI Coding Agent in 2026?
summary: Feature/pricing comparison of Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot; explicitly not a benchmark.

assertions.quote: Notice what is missing, a universal winner

verdicts.note: By 2026 the major tools all offer agents, CLIs, cloud runs and review; differences are workflow and pricing more than capability.

assertions.quote: for automation and parallel delegation, Codex has one of the clearest product visions

verdicts.note: Codex does emphasize parallel cloud tasks and automations, but Cursor, Copilot and Claude Code offer similar features; 'strongest' is unproven.

assertions.quote: a programmable senior pair living in your terminal

verdicts.note: Hooks, subagents, headless/SDK mode and MCP make Claude Code highly scriptable; accurate description of its design focus.

assertions.quote: Cursor is arguably the cleanest fit

verdicts.note: Cursor's indexing and model choice are accurate; 'most integrated' is a taste judgment and competitors have closed gaps.

assertions.quote: at $10, it's paid individual tier is the cheapest headline subscription

verdicts.note: Copilot Pro's $10 tier is the cheapest headline price and GitHub integration is real; 'best fit' depends on team needs.

assertions.quote: Treat the sticker price as the entry point, not a promise of unlimited heavy automation

verdicts.note: Agentic usage is metered or rate-limited across vendors; heavy users routinely hit limits or pay usage overages.
